section_summary.extract_value: This section reports a single-study path analysis testing relationships among external shame (OAS), self-compassion (SCS_SC), BMI, and body appreciation (BAS-2). The final model (with one non-significant path removed) explained 13% of SCS_SC and 49% of BAS-2 variance, showed excellent fit, found a direct negative effect of BMI on BAS-2 (standardized β = -0.27), and demonstrated invariance across male (n = 44) and female (n = 111) subgroups.

section_summary.extract_value: This section reports path-analytic results testing a theoretical model (initially 18 parameters) explaining 13% of variance in self-compassion (SCS_SC) and 49% in body appreciation (BAS-2), with one nonsignificant direct path (BMI → SCS_SC) removed and the readjusted model showing excellent fit. External shame (OAS) had strong negative direct effects on self-compassion and body appreciation and an indirect negative effect on body appreciation mediated by self-compassion; self-compassion was positively associated with BAS-2, and BMI showed a negative direct effect on BAS-2 (standardized β = −0.27). A multigroup invariance analysis across the sample's males (n = 44) and females (n = 111) indicated no differences in factor weights (model invariant). No study label such as 'Study 1' or 'Experiment' is mentioned in this section.
section_summary.evidence_source: Key sentences: 'This model explained 13% of the variance of self-compassion (SCS_SC) and 49% of the variance of body appreciation (BAS-2).'; 'Due to the non-significance of one of the paths, that is the direct effect of BMI on SCS_SC ... this path was eliminated and the model was readjusted.'; 'body mass index revealed a direct negative effect on BAS-2 ... β = −0.27.'; 'Finally, a multigroup analysis ... sample's males and females.'
